From: D. Scott,  CARLISLE

My equipment consists of a Spec-
trum +, Interface 1, two micro-
drives and a Brother M-1009
Printer. I would like to upgrade
as I could use a lot more
memory. I have my name down for
a COUPE (if it ever appears as
the production date is put
forward another month with each
anouncement from MGT).

I am now considering purchasing
a Spectrum 128 if I can find one
or a Spectrum +2,which I believe
will accept the Interface 1 and
microdrives.

The other alternative would be a
Spectrum +2 and Plus D with twin

disc drives. I would appreciate
your advice. I am secretary for
two organizations and have the
records for both as Tasword 3
text files. This is useful as I
can chop and change fonts for
differing outputs and layouts in
connection with the organiz-
ations. The problem is the files
are getting so long that I am
having to break them up into
groups e.g. A to D, E to I etc.

There is a little problem with
the new COL80 PLUS. I can have
80 columns of Pica print or 80
columns of condensed which
should, of course, print as 137
columns. Any suggestions?

                 D. Scott

To: D. Scott from Brian

I'm not sure TASWORD PLUS 2 will
give you much bigger text files.
Can anyone with a Tas128 let us
know the maximum file size?

I would consider looking at say,
MASTERFILE for record-keeping as
it is more flexible and uses
memory more efficiently than a
straight text file.A lot depends
on the nature of the data.A very
simple BASIC database may be all
you need. If you send me one of
your textfiles (with dummy data
if the records are confidential)
I could advise on this or even
write the program myself (for
inclusion in OUTLET). It may be
possible to transfer the data
without typing it in again.

The problem with COL80+ is that
versions of Interface 1 later
than my own have an additional
system variable to set a maximum
column width. This seems totally
pointless to me as it appears to
serve no purpose other than to
be an extra restriction! Surely
everyone uses printer codes to
set up margins if needed?

Correct this by using BREAK in
COL80+, enter LIST 9896 and then
EDIT. Type in POKE 23729,P: at
the start of the line and then
ENTER again. Re-SAVE the program
with RUN 9980. Disciple users
will also need to amend the line
but use: POKE @5,P instead and
Kempston E users: POKE 23679,P

                    - Brian

             - Brian

From BoB Smith

Dear OUTLET readers,
(and Ron and Brian)

Before I get to my question let
me say thanks for a great magaz-
ine. Its a real pleasure to see
it go from strength to strength.

Now down to business. I have a
CITIZEN 120D dot matrix printer
and I am looking for a way to
make it back-feed the paper. By
that I mean roll the paper in
the opposite direction to
normal. I know that the printer
will do that as it does it in
NLQ mode when double-height
characters are selected for part
of a line of text.

For example if I wanted the word
HELLO printed double-height with
"campers" printed next to it but
single height then my printer
prints the whole of HELLO, back
feeds the correct amount to line
up campers and then prints that.

I have scoured the manual only
to find no mention of this func-
tion. I have tried some codes at
random also to no avail. Anyone
out there have any ideas?

I'm of the opinion that if the
printer can do it when IT wants
to then I can tell it to do it
when I want it to. All I need to
do is find out what to tell it.

I await your replies with hope.
                        - BoB .

To BoB Smith from Ron


The only suggestion I can offer
is to try the command for
reversing the paper feed on the
Kaga Taxan printer, which is -

LPRINT 27;"j";CHR$ n

where n is the number of reverse
line feeds required. Any oher
suggestions from readers?

Ron.

From Lee Jon Powis, BOURNVILLE

I am unable to return to BASIC
with a recent code program of
mine - why I don't know!

i) Interrupts are in normal mode
and enabled.

ii) The index, i, r and exchange
registers haven't been touched.

iii) The stack isn't overwritten
and, even if I PUSHed/POPed too
much, SP was stored and then
collected on return to BASIC
(which doesn't happen!) so I
should be alright. Can you solve
this?
      Thanks,
             L.J. Powis

To Lee Powis from Brian
Without seeing the program I can
only guess. Although you stored
the SP position you don't say
you MOVED it. Your program may
conceivably POP too many values
off the STACK and PUSH some new
one(s) back.Even if you point SP
to the address where it started,
the values on the STACK above it
may have been altered.Try moving
SP to a completely new position
-well away from the old STACK at
the start of your code and then
restore it at the end.

You need to send a blank Opus or
Disciple disc or cartridge (not
available on tape or +3) to get
the "free demo" we advertise (to
newcomers only)
                      - Brian

From: Terry Hayes
I have been learning m/c and can
follow most programs through
after a bit of studying, however
I'm having problems with certain
statements in your listing as,
for example,DATA NOT PI, SGN PI,
PRINT AT PI*PI, INK NOT PI, CODE
"#".Others are VAL"9E3" or 1e3
or RESTORE 9E3.

In Spectrum BASIC,numbers not in
quotes are followed by 6 bytes
not shown in the listing. 0 uses
7 bytes! Using NOT PI(=0)saves 5
bytes, SGN PI=1, PI*PI counts as
10(in a PRINT AT statement)etc.
9e3 or 9E3 means 9+3 zeros= 9000
See also OUTCLASS 5 on saving
memory and BASICMEM in Issue 18.
                     - Brian

From Ian Miller, LONDON SE9

I notice you're compiling a UDG
catalogue. Do you realize there
are 18,446,744,070,000,000,000
possible UDGs! How do you SAVE
and use UDGs made in Utility 1?

Enter SAVE "NAME" CODE A,B where
A is the low byte+256 times the
high byte (shown in UTILITY 1)
and B is 768 for a font and 168
for UDGS (152 on 128K).

To use: enter LOAD "NAME" CODE
and POKE 23606,low : POKE 23607,
high minus 1 (font) and POKE
23675,high :POKE 23676,low(UDGs)
(normally address 65368). Use
CLEAR A-1 (or less) first and
always keep your fingers crossed
                       - Brian

From: E. Taylor, SEAHAM

I would like to ask a question
on a number of older programs,
such as GAUNTLET. How do you get
rid of line 0?



Enter: LET PROG=PEEK 23635+256*
PEEK 23636: POKE PROG+1,1

This changes the line number to
1 which you can delete in the
usual way by typing: 1 ENTER. I
have no idea,however,what line 0
does in any of the programs you
have so I take no responsibility

From Alistair McColl, CLYDEBANK


Dear Brian & Ron,

The saga of my printout problem
and CAL-PLAN has been solved at
last by using some of the info
from OUTLET and some from my
printer manual. I have come up
with the following in line 9895
after LPRINT CHR$ VAL"27";"@":
add- LPRINT CHR$ 27;"C";CHR$ 70:


Hey presto CAL-PLAN now prints
out on exact A4 size paper. I
hope this works for Scott Brown
and anyone else who has had this
problem.

I thank you for passing on my
printer query to Mike Haine
(OUTPRINT on A4) and to Mike for
his advice. As stated when 64955
is PEEKed, 9 is displayed but I
don't seem to be putting the
POKE 64955,15 in the right way
because when I make a SAVE or do
a print-out, 64955 has reverted
back to 9. Should the POKE be
inserted into a line in the
program listing or should it be
inserted by BREAK, POKE 64955,15
ENTER?

While I am on about A4 printouts
how about pointing me in the
right direction to alter OUTDEX
to printout A4 sheets instead of
continuous?

Your editorial in Issue 24 asks
for ideas re:programs etc., well
one program I would like to see
is a program that you could file
corrections and tips into then
printout (A4 size of course).How
often has one said, "I have seen
that somewhere..."then proceeded
to search through all the
issues.I would suggest along the
lines of OUTDEX but with input
as required by oneself. This
program would be able to file
subject (e.g. MERGE), issue No.,
section (e.g. OUTCLASS) and page
No. of section together with a
description (e.g. How to use
MERGE).
          Yours faithfully,

            Alistair McColl

To Alistair McColl from Brian

Ah!I see where the POKE is going
wrong!When the program is run it
moves the code up again from the
REM. Put the POKE in line 400
AFTER the GO SUB 9101 then try.

To alter OUTDEX for true A4 try
your own mod but put it in line
9881 (if Kempston E), 9887 (if
microdrive or Opus) or 9890 if
Disciple and put it after the
LPRINT CHR$ 27;"@" as before.

Les Tyler is looking at an index
system but I suspect everyone
has a different idea of what is
wanted. Perhaps your idea of a
blank database the user himself
can enter the info HE/SHE wants
is the answer...       - Brian.
